I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It builds at 606 bytes min+gzip, with 95 bytes of my own code. Type checking reports no errors in `out/`.

I did not run an equivalence test against the original. The original needs lodash, which isn't installed, and `src/module.ts` itself fails to type-check here for that reason. I couldn't print a size for the original either, because `npm run size` with no argument crashed before printing, so I can't confirm the own-code allowance (check 4). Reading the code, I expect results to match the original for the input range.

- **`byId`:** it uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`. When two rows share an id, the last one wins, same as lodash.
- **`totalAge`:** it uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`. That version only takes a function, not the `'age'` string lodash accepted, so the adapter is `(row) => row.age`. An empty array returns 0, same as lodash.
- **`isBlank`:** `es-toolkit` has no `isEmpty` (only `isEmptyObject`, which doesn't cover strings, arrays and primitives). I used `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`, which handles null, booleans, numbers, strings, arrays and objects the way lodash does. No lodash import remains.

The exported signatures, `Row` and `Config` are unchanged.
